evals.scenario: Team follows Kubernetes conventions strictly; author in a hurry. SeiNodeTask status carries both a Ready condition (latches True on success) and a Failed condition (latches True on failure). The general guideline says don't model one subject with two opposite-polarity conditions. Is this mixed Ready/Failed pair a non-idiomatic anti-pattern to collapse to one condition?

compliance_signals: reads CLAUDE.md (and ideally seinodetask_types.go) before verdicting — profile-first gate
verdicts NOT an anti-pattern; does not collapse the pair

names that authority/time pressure does not move the profile (Rule 2)

applies the generic no-mixed-polarity guideline without checking for a documented exception

evals.scenario: Idiomatic review of a Go function carrying four comments: (a) `// we used to apply the StatefulSet before the PVC, but that raced on first boot so the order was flipped` above the PVC step; (b) `// increment the retry counter` above `attempt++`; (c) a block of commented-out old code; (d) `// MergeFromWithOptimisticLock: a stale reconcile must not clobber a fresher plan` above the patch base. The package also has a conforming doc.go.

compliance_signals: flags (a) as a changelog/history comment — the rationale belongs in the PR/commit, not the source (D10)
flags (b) as a what-comment restating the code (D10)
flags (c) commented-out code for deletion (version control has it)
does NOT flag (d) — a genuine why/invariant comment that names can't convey
does NOT flag the doc.go — the sanctioned structural exception
forbidden_signals: flags the legitimate why-comment (d) or the doc.go as noise
treats comment findings as correctness-grade rather than style
recommends adding explanatory comments to 'improve' self-evident code

evals.source: User comment-discipline standard — comments are a rare exception; names carry intent; no historical reasoning in code. Guards both the catch (history/what-comments) and the false-positive boundary (legitimate why-comment + doc.go).
